name: vscode-sqlprompt
description: SQL Server IntelliSense - schema-aware autocomplete like Redgate SQL Prompt

sqlPrompt.trace.server.description: Traces the communication between VS Code and the language server.

sqlPrompt.snippets.shortcuts.markdownDescription:
Statement shortcuts expanded by the completion list, added to the built-in ones (`ssf`, `scf`, `sct`, `st10`, `st100`, `ap`, `av`, `af`; `st<N>` always expands to `SELECT TOP N * FROM`). Key: the shortcut (letters, digits, `_`); value: the text to insert, `
` for a new line and `$CURSOR$` for where the cursor ends up. Redefine a built-in shortcut to change it, or set it to an empty string to remove it. Example: `{ "sd": "SELECT DISTINCT ", "bt": "BEGIN TRAN;
$CURSOR$
ROLLBACK;" }`

enumDescriptions: Turn off the mssql extension's suggestions once, in your User settings: no project file is touched.
Turn off the mssql extension's suggestions in this workspace's settings (written once).
Leave the mssql extension's suggestions on: both lists appear together.
sqlPrompt.suppressMssqlIntellisense.markdownDescription: Where SQL Prompt turns off the mssql extension's own suggestions (`mssql.intelliSense.enableSuggestions`), so that only SQL Prompt completions appear. The setting is written once and never toggled on connect or disconnect. Connection features (Script As, Alter Procedure, etc.) are unaffected. Older `true`/`false` values still work as `user`/`off`.

sqlPrompt.formatting.stylesFolder.description: Absolute path to the folder containing SQL Prompt style files (.json). All .json files in the folder are loaded as formatting profiles.

sqlPrompt.formatting.activeStyle.description: Name of the active formatting style (the style's metadata.name, or the filename without .json). Set via the 'SQL Prompt: Select Formatting Style' command.

enumDescriptions: Built-in TypeScript formatter (fallback when .NET is not available).
Default: .NET engine built on Microsoft ScriptDom, aiming at SQL Prompt parity. Requires the .NET 10 runtime.
sqlPrompt.formatting.engine.markdownDescription: Formatting engine. `dotnet` (default) parses the script with Microsoft ScriptDom like SQL Prompt does and needs the .NET 10 runtime, downloaded automatically by the *.NET Install Tool* extension (an extension dependency) unless `sqlPrompt.formatting.dotnetPath` is set. If the engine cannot start, the built-in `legacy` formatter is used.

sqlPrompt.formatting.dotnetPath.description: Optional path of the dotnet executable used by the .NET formatting engine.

scripts.vscode:prepublish: npm run build:engine && npm run webpack
scripts.postinstall: cd client && npm install && cd ../server && npm install
